title: At a Restaurant
description: Learn how to order food, ask for the menu, and pay the bill in Hindi.

exercises.explanation: Restaurant essentials — 'chahiye' (I want/need) and 'bill lao' (bring the bill) are your two most important phrases.

exercises.question: How do you ask for the bill in Hindi?
exercises.explanation: 'Bill lao' = bring the bill. 'Lao' is a casual imperative meaning 'bring'. More polite: 'bill laiye'.
'Mujhe khaana chahiye' = I want to eat / I want food. 'Khaana' = food or the act of eating.
'Mujhe menu chahiye' = I want the menu. 'Chahiye' expresses wanting or needing something.
'Bahut achhaa' = very good/tasty. More specific: 'bahut swaadisht' = very delicious.

exercises.question: How do you ask 'what vegetables do you have?'
exercises.explanation: 'Kya sabzi hai?' = what vegetables do you have? / is there a vegetable dish?
'Ek roti aur ek dal chahiye' = I want one roti and one dal.
'Kya veg khaana hai?' = do you have vegetarian food? 'Veg' is universally understood across India.
exercises.hint: sounds like: kyaa vej khaa-naa hai
